title: Exercises
html:
Do these in your Week 2 workbook and bring it to the session. Allow about 60 minutes.

Open the workbook here. Google Docs will ask you to make a copy, so you need to be signed in to a Google account.

The workbook takes you from reading about cost-effectiveness analysis to doing a simple one. It has five parts:

  • Part 1: Build a simple estimate (about 20 min). You follow a worked example for bed nets, then make your own estimate for vitamin A supplementation. All the inputs are given. The formula is: cost per death averted = cost per person reached ÷ (baseline mortality rate × efficacy).

  • Part 2: Find the same numbers in GiveWell’s model (about 20 min). You open GiveWell’s spreadsheet for Malaria Consortium and find five inputs. The workbook tells you which tab and column to use and what each term means.

  • Part 3: Stress-test an input (about 10 min). Change one input by 50% in each direction and see how far the answer moves.

  • Part 4: Spot the weakest link (about 5 min). Say what you would most want to check before trusting GiveWell’s recommendation.

  • Part 5: Reflect (about 5 min).

GiveWell’s spreadsheet is large and full of jargon. You are not expected to understand all of it. You only need the five rows the workbook points you to.
